title: Degree-zero part of injective Cech augmentation
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U_i an arbitrary open cover of X, and J an injective sheaf of O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let C(U,J) be the Cech cochain complex of the presheaf of global-section-ring modules [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. Global sections are the evaluation functor of [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Let b be a cochain map from the single-term complex J(X)[0] to C(U,J), whose degree-zero component is the canonical restriction map into the product over Fin 1-tuples, preceded by the identity restriction-of-scalars identification at X. The structure-sheaf map from X to itself is identified with the identity ring homomorphism, by a supplied proof ht of that equality. Then the homology map of b in degree zero is an isomorphism. This concerns one injective module, with no injective resolution or total complex.

source.place: Tag 01EP (lemma-injective-trivial-cech), degree-zero and positive-degree clauses, as used in the augmented-row argument of Tag 01EQ (lemma-cech-cohomology).

proof.text: Identify categorical products of opens with finite intersections and products of modules with families of sections. The first Cech differential is the difference of the two restrictions on every pairwise overlap. Its kernel therefore consists of compatible families; the sheaf gluing axiom gives a unique section on their union. By hU the union is X. Restriction from J(X) to this kernel is therefore a linear bijection.

Both complexes have zero incoming boundaries in degree zero. The source zero homology is its only term and the target zero homology is the kernel just identified. ht gives the identity scalar identification and hb identifies the induced map with restriction. Thus the map is an isomorphism. For an empty cover hU forces X empty and the empty-cover sheaf axiom identifies J(X) with zero, as is the empty product in the target. Injectivity is unnecessary in this degree.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01EP; the source-library flasque route for positive degree, and sheaf gluing in degree zero. T2 second reading, 2026-10-12.

from.place: Strict degree part of the augmented Cech quasi-isomorphism

lean.statement:
theorem injectiveModuleCechAugmentation_quasiIsoAt_zero {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u}
    (U : ι → X.Opens) (hU : iSup U = ⊤) (J : X.Modules) [Injective J]
    (ht : (X.ringCatSheaf.obj.map (isTerminalTop.op.to (op ⊤))).hom =
      RingHom.id Γ(X, ⊤))
    (b : (CochainComplex.single₀ (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, ⊤))).obj
        ((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).obj J) ⟶
      (CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor U).obj J.presheafModuleCat)
    (hb : b.f 0 =
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalarsId'App
        (X.ringCatSheaf.obj.map (isTerminalTop.op.to (op ⊤))).hom ht
        (J.val.obj (op ⊤))).inv ≫
      Pi.lift fun y : Fin 1 → ι =>
        J.presheafModuleCat.map (homOfLE (le_top (a := ∏ᶜ fun l => U (y l)))).op) :
    QuasiIsoAt b 0
